messages:
elena: Thanks everyone for joining the runtime Q&A. Quick follow-up thread — two asks: 1) clarify kernel prioritization timeline, 2) how batching/caching changes map to SLAs for Dedicated customers.

devon: Good recap. Kernel team will publish a short plan by EOD Fri. Primary focus: attention kernel refactor -> reduce p95 for long sequences.

jia: To add: we're targeting 20% p95 reduction on 8k contexts on A100-class infra with merged attention improvements.

sam: How does that interact with continuous batching? Will we see higher variability due to batching windows?

jia: Good question. Short answer: batching windows tuned per-service. Longer batches improve throughput but we keep tail latency by reserving a small low-latency pool.

maria: For Dedicated customers, can we document expected delta in SLOs if they enable aggressive batching? Some customers asked about this.

devon: Yes — the plan is to provide a 'throughput-optimized' config with explicit tradeoffs and observable metrics. Docs + console toggles in next ship.

sam: Any changes to KV cache TTL or prefix caching we should be aware of? We saw cache thrashing on chat workloads last week.

jia: We'll increase default KV cache size and add an LRU-aware eviction metric. Also a config for per-model prefix cache ttl.

elena: Can we get a short benchmark artifact? A link that PMs and AE can share.

devon: Will publish a results doc + runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-kernel-179

maria: Is there a migration path for Private on-prem customers without rolling restarts?

jia: We plan a canary rollout strategy with model-version aliasing so we can migrate traffic gradually, no full restarts required.

sam: Thx — and FYI PR #4321 adds a microbenchmark harness for quantized kernels.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary started for kernel-refactor v2 on staging at 1792057950 :rocket: \n
elena: Awesome. If you have follow-ups, drop them here or ping me. We'll reconvene in infra sync next Tue.
